basis.note: Topic list and order from the UIL high-school chart. The short-cut techniques and the estimation topic are a house list. Unit 6 goes past the chart: the cover-up items follow an MIT 18.03 course note and the one-a-minute integration pace follows the MIT Integration Bee qualifier; which results belong in unit 6 is a house list. Pace comes from the UIL rules (7.5 s a problem) and the English multiplication tables check (6 s a fact).

big_ideas.title: See the structure before you compute
big_ideas.text: Most mental calculation is noticing that the numbers in front of you are a special case of an identity (a difference of squares, a common factor, a number near a round one) and letting the identity do the work.

big_ideas.title: A small set of facts, recalled at once
big_ideas.text: Squares, cubes, powers of two, fraction-percent pairs and unit factors are worth knowing cold, because every short-cut bottoms out in one of them and a fact that takes five seconds to rebuild breaks the chain.

big_ideas.title: An estimate is an answer
big_ideas.text: A number good to a few percent, with the right order of magnitude, is often all a decision needs, and it is the check that catches a slipped decimal in an exact calculation.

practices.title: Compute in the head
practices.text: Hold intermediate results in working memory and say the answer most significant digit first.

practices.title: Choose the short-cut
practices.text: Recognise which identity or known fact fits the numbers before starting.

practices.title: Estimate and check
practices.text: Round deliberately, track the direction of the error, and test an exact answer against its size.

topics.title: Operations on integers, fractions and decimals

los.do: Take a fraction of a whole number by dividing first.
ek: p/q of n: divide by q, then multiply by p.

los.do: Add and subtract multi-digit numbers left to right, and subtract from a power of ten by complements.
ek: Say the large part of the answer first; 1000 − n is nines-and-a-ten on the digits.
Slide both numbers so the one taken away is round (541 − 229 = 542 − 230); count up when the two are close.

los.do: Evaluate a short expression with mixed operations in the right order.
ek: Products and quotients before sums and differences, then left to right.

los.do: Spot a common factor and add before multiplying.
ek: ab + ac = a(b + c); look for sums that make 10, 50 or 100.

los.do: Compare two fractions by cross-multiplying.
ek: a/b > c/d exactly when ad > bc (positive denominators).

los.do: Multiply by 11, 25, 5, 99 and 101 by rewriting the multiplier.
Multiply two numbers just under 100 from their shortfalls.
Multiply two-digit numbers that share a tens digit and whose ones digits sum to 10, or that sit evenly around a round number.
Double one factor and halve the other to make a round number.
ek: ab = (a/2)(2b); a factor ending in 5 doubles to a multiple of 10.

los.do: Divide by 5 and 25 by rewriting the divisor, and by a two-digit number in stages.
ek: ÷5 = ×2 ÷10; ÷25 = ×4 ÷100; ÷35 = ÷5 then ÷7. Multiply back to check.

los.do: Divide by a decimal by moving both decimal points until the divisor is whole.
ek: 12.6 ÷ 0.35 = 1260 ÷ 35: dollars ÷ dollars per minute becomes cents ÷ cents per minute.

los.do: Square a number ending in 5, or near 50 or 100, from its pattern.
Square any two-digit number by sliding to a multiple of ten.
ek: n² = (n − d)(n + d) + d².

los.do: Recall the percent form of the common fractions, and use it to take a percent of a number.
Convert between common units of length, capacity, weight and time, including square and cubic units.
ek: 12 in/ft, 3 ft/yd, 5280 ft/mi, 4 qt/gal, 2 pt/qt, 16 oz/lb; area factors are squared, volume factors cubed.

los.do: Read a Roman numeral.
ek: I V X L C D M = 1 5 10 50 100 500 1000; a smaller symbol before a larger one is subtracted.

los.do: Find the GCD and LCM of two numbers under 100.
ek: The GCD divides the difference; LCM = product ÷ GCD.

los.do: Take a percent of a number by swapping or building from 10%, and apply a percent increase or decrease.
ek: a% of b = b% of a; a change of p% multiplies by 1 ± p/100.

los.do: Find a mean with a focus number and the median of a short unsorted list.
ek: Mean = guess + (sum of deviations)/n; the median survives striking extremes in pairs.

los.do: Sum the first n integers, the first n odd numbers, or a short arithmetic series.
ek: 1 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2; 1 + 3 + … + (2n − 1) = n²; a series sums to (number of terms)(average of first and last).

los.do: Find a remainder on division by 3, 4, 9 or 11 from the digits.
ek: Mod 3 and 9: digit sum. Mod 4: last two digits. Mod 11: alternating digit sum from the right.

los.do: Find a sale price or similar everyday percent amount.
ek: Pay (100 − p)% of the price; build from 10%.

los.do: Count the divisors of a number, and sum them, from its prime factorisation.
ek: d(n) = ∏(eᵢ + 1); σ is multiplicative, with σ(pᵏ) = 1 + p + … + pᵏ.

los.do: Estimate a product, a quotient or a square root to within 5 percent.
ek: Round in opposite directions for a product and in the same direction for a quotient; √(a² + h) ≈ a + h/(2a).

los.do: Recall the powers of 2 to 2¹² and the cubes to 12³.
Evaluate an expression at given values without writing it out.
ek: Substitute, then use the order of operations.

los.do: Solve a one-step word problem (ages, rates, coins) mentally.
ek: Name the unknown and undo one operation.

los.do: Give the additive or multiplicative inverse of an integer, fraction or mixed number.
ek: Additive inverses sum to 0; multiplicative inverses multiply to 1.

los.do: Evaluate an expression with absolute values.
ek: |x| is the distance from 0.

los.do: Solve a proportion by scaling or cross-multiplying.
ek: a/b = c/d means ad = bc.

los.do: Find the root of a perfect square or cube from its size and last digit.
ek: Bracket between squares of tens; the last digit narrows the ones digit.

los.do: Count subsets, and elements of unions and intersections.
ek: A set of n elements has 2ⁿ subsets; |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B|.

los.do: Convert a short numeral from another base to base 10.
ek: Multiply by the base and add the next digit, left to right.

los.do: Solve a one- or two-step linear equation mentally.
ek: Undo operations in reverse order.

los.do: Find x + y or x − y from a 2 × 2 system by adding or subtracting the equations.
ek: Often the combination asked for falls out without solving for each variable.

los.do: Write a repeating decimal as a fraction.
ek: A repeating block of k digits sits over k nines.

los.do: Find the remainder of a sum or product from the remainders of its parts.
ek: Remainders add and multiply (mod m).

topics.title: Perimeter and area of polygons and circles

los.do: Find the perimeter or area of a rectangle, triangle, trapezoid or circle from its dimensions.
ek: A = bh, ½bh, ½(b₁ + b₂)h, πr².

los.do: Find the next or the n-th term of an arithmetic or geometric sequence.
ek: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d; aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹.

los.do: Give the sum or product of the roots of a quadratic or cubic from its coefficients.
ek: For ax² + bx + c: sum −b/a, product c/a.

los.do: Simplify a product or quotient of powers by moving to a common base.
ek: aᵐaⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; 4 = 2², 8 = 2³.

los.do: Complete a Pythagorean triple or a 30-60-90 or 45-45-90 triangle.
Find a slope, midpoint, distance or intercept from two points or an equation.
ek: m = Δy/Δx; midpoint averages the coordinates.

los.do: Find an interior or exterior angle, or the number of diagonals, of a regular polygon.
ek: Exterior angle 360°/n; diagonals n(n − 3)/2.

los.do: Solve a linear inequality or count its integer solutions.
ek: Multiplying by a negative reverses the inequality.

los.do: Use an angle, chord, tangent or similarity fact to find a length or angle.
ek: Inscribed angle = half the arc; similar figures scale areas by k².

los.do: Find a value from a direct or inverse variation.
ek: y = kx or y = k/x; find k first, or scale.

topics.title: Sequences and series, finite and infinite

los.do: Sum an infinite geometric series.
Multiply two complex numbers or find a modulus or a power of i.
ek: i² = −1; |a + bi|² = a² + b².

los.do: Evaluate a logarithm of an exact power.
ek: log_b(bᵏ) = k.

los.do: Evaluate a small combination, permutation or factorial ratio.
Give the probability or odds of a simple event with dice, coins or cards.
ek: Odds in favour = successes : failures.

los.do: Read a centre, vertex, focus or axis length from a conic in standard form.
ek: Circle (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²; ellipse axes 2a and 2b.

los.do: Give a coefficient or the sum of coefficients of a binomial expansion.
ek: Coefficients are C(n, k); their sum is the expansion at x = y = 1.

los.do: Add, subtract or multiply two short numerals in another base.
ek: Carry at the base instead of at ten.

los.do: Use Vieta's relations to find symmetric expressions in the roots.
ek: r₁² + r₂² = (r₁ + r₂)² − 2r₁r₂.

los.do: Find the n-th triangular, pentagonal or hexagonal number.
ek: Triangular n(n + 1)/2; pentagonal n(3n − 1)/2; hexagonal n(2n − 1).

los.do: Find the volume or surface area of a prism, cylinder, cone or sphere, in terms of π where needed.
ek: V = πr²h, ⅓πr²h, ⁴⁄₃πr³; sphere area 4πr².

los.do: Evaluate a floor expression, including of negative numbers.
ek: ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer not above x; ⌊−2.3⌋ = −3.

los.do: Find the remainder of a polynomial on division by x − a.
ek: The remainder is p(a).

los.do: Recall exact trig values at the special angles and use basic identities.
ek: sin and cos of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° and their reflections; sin² + cos² = 1.

los.do: Evaluate a 2 × 2 or simple 3 × 3 determinant.
ek: ad − bc.

los.do: Find an entry of a matrix sum, product or inverse.
ek: Row times column.

los.do: Find a dot product or a magnitude.
ek: u·v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂.

los.do: Evaluate f(g(a)) for simple f and g.
ek: Work from the inside out.

los.do: Convert a fraction to or from a numeral with digits after the point in another base.
ek: Places after the point are negative powers of the base.

los.do: Convert a point between polar and rectangular form at a special angle.
ek: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ.

los.do: State the excluded value or the range of a simple rational, radical or quadratic function.
ek: Denominator ≠ 0; radicand ≥ 0; a quadratic's range starts or ends at its vertex.

los.do: Evaluate a sum, product or power modulo m.
ek: Reduce before multiplying; powers cycle.

los.do: Evaluate a limit of a rational function at a point or at infinity by inspection.
ek: At infinity compare leading terms; at a 0/0 point cancel the common factor.

los.do: Evaluate the derivative of a polynomial or basic function at a point.
ek: Power rule term by term.

los.do: Give the slope of the tangent to a curve at a point.
ek: It is f′ at that x.

los.do: Read the asymptotes of a rational function from its formula.
ek: Vertical where the reduced denominator is 0; horizontal from the leading terms.

los.do: Find where a polynomial's derivative is zero.
ek: Set f′ = 0 and factor.

los.do: Find the maximum or minimum value of a quadratic or a simple cubic on an interval.
ek: A quadratic's extreme is at x = −b/(2a).

los.do: Evaluate a definite integral of a polynomial with easy limits.
ek: Antidifferentiate term by term; use symmetry for odd and even integrands.

los.do: Evaluate f⁻¹(a) for a linear or simple rational f without finding the inverse formula.
ek: Solve f(x) = a.

los.do: Read off one coefficient of a partial-fraction decomposition with distinct linear factors by covering up.
ek: Cover the factor, substitute its root into what is left.

los.do: Use cover-up where it still works: the top power of a repeated factor, and a linear factor beside an irreducible quadratic.
ek: Cover-up gives the highest-power coefficient only; the rest need one more step.

los.do: Integrate a basic function of a linear inside (cos kx, sin kx, e^kx, (kx + b)^n, 1/(kx + b)) by guessing the shape and fixing the constant.
ek: Differentiate the guess in your head; divide by whatever constant it throws out.

los.do: Spot an integrand of the form f(g(x))·g′(x) up to a constant and write its antiderivative.
ek: f′/f integrates to ln f; u^n du to u^(n+1)/(n+1); x·e^(kx²) to an exponential.

los.do: Write the derivative of a one-layer composite or a power-times-exponential product without intermediate steps.
ek: Outside derivative with the inside untouched, times the inside derivative.

los.do: Find the eigenvalues of a 2 × 2 matrix from its trace and determinant.
ek: Sum = trace, product = determinant.

los.do: Classify y″ + by′ + cy = 0 by comparing b² with 4c, and choose the trial form for an exponential forcing term.
ek: b² > 4c overdamped, = critical, < underdamped; multiply the trial by x once per time the exponent is a characteristic root.
